body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvādikarmika-mārgāvatāra-deśanā</s> (Instruction on Entering the Path for the Beginning <s>Bodhisattva</s>)

children.translated_text: That which destroys misfortune in <s>saṃsāra</s> and grants the prosperity of liberation,
the jewel of all in the ten directions—I pay homage to the feet of the <s>Guru</s>. // 1 //

body.text: iha yaḥ svabhāvato mahākaruṇāprajñāvān mahāyānagotrīyaḥ, yaśca pūrvajanmasu mahāyānabhāvukaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsārasunirviṇṇacittaḥ maraṇānusmṛtikaśca samastabāhyādhyātmika-vastusvalpābhiniveśaḥ, 'ekasatkalyāṇamitrata ekāviparyastamārgaśravaṇe kiṃ na syāt? ahamekaṃ santaṃ anveṣyāmi' - evaṃ cintayan saḥ kalyāṇamitrānurupaṃ gurumanviṣya anyatra nirdiṣṭavat triśaraṇagamanaviśiṣṭaḥ, anantagatīḥ viṣayīkṛtya, sadāśayaḥ, anuttaramahābodhāvasādhāraṇacittotpādaḥ, sadadhyāśayaḥ, māyāśāṭhyarahitabodhiprasthānamahācittoḥ bodhisattvaśīlasya triśikṣāṃ suṣṭhu gṛhṇīyāt / tataḥ śvaśvapacadāsasaṃjñakasya māyāśāṭhyarahitasya tasya bodhisattvasya saṃbhāramārgīyatvād ahorātraṃ kāya-vāk-cittasamastakarmāṇi na vyarthāni bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Here, one who is by nature endowed with great compassion and wisdom, belonging to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage (<s>gotra</s>), who in previous births was a person devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, whose mind is thoroughly weary of <s>saṃsāra</s>, who practices mindfulness of death, and who has little attachment to all external and internal objects—thinking 'Would it not be good to have one true spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) and to hear one unerring path? I shall seek out one virtuous person'—having thus reflected and seeking a <s>guru</s> who is a fitting spiritual friend, distinguished by taking the <s>triśaraṇa</s> (three refuges) as instructed elsewhere, taking all destinies as one's concern, with good intention, with the uncommon generation of the mind of unsurpassed great awakening (<s>anuttara-mahābodhi</s>), with genuine resolve, and with the great aspiration for setting forth toward awakening free from deceit and cunning—one should properly take up the three trainings (<s>triśikṣā</s>) of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct. Then, for that <s>bodhisattva</s> free from deceit and cunning—even if designated as a <s>śvapaca</s> (outcaste) servant—because of being on the <s>saṃbhāramārga</s> (path of accumulation), all actions of body, speech, and mind day and night are not in vain.

body.text: evaṃ tena cittena bhojanamātrājñānam, indriyadvārasaṃvaraṇam, aṇumātre 'pyavadye bhayadarśanam, aharniśaṃ yogañca āpādayet / tataḥ śvāsapraśvāsamapi parārtham abhilaṣitukāmaḥ saḥ pañcamaprahara utthāya, uccāraprasrāvatyāgādicaryā sunirvartya madhyadeśapratyantajanapadaviśeṣe snātvā, samastagatīḥ avalambya caturapramāṇairbodhau cittamutpādya, triratnapratimāsamakṣaṃ sulipya sugandhapuṣpaprakaraṃ suvikīrya tadagrato bhūmau jānunī saṃsthāpya, kṛtāñjaliḥ daśadiglokadhāta-samastabuddha-samastadharmamahāyānasaṃghasamakṣaṃ ca asaṃkhyānirvācyakāyavyūhān nirmāya teṣāñcaikaikam caraṇayoḥ supraṇamet / tān aparimitavipulāprameyāmiṣapūjayā pūjayet / tataḥ pratikāyaṃ anirvacanīyamukhāni pratimukhaṃ cānirvacanīyajihvā nirmāya, svaparapāpān aśeṣān diśet / svaparapuṇyāni cānumodayet / aciram abhisambodhiprāptān buddhān bhagavato dharmacakrapravartanāya adhyeṣayet / ye dharmacakraṃ pravartya āyuḥ saṃskārān parijihīrṣante, (tān) āsaṃsāram aparinirvāṇāya prārthayeta / teṣāṃ samastakuśalānām anuttarasamyaksambodhau pariṇāmanāṃ kuryāt / yathā sūtre āgatāni tathā pratyaṅgapadāni savistaraṃ paṭhet /
body.translated_text: With such a mind, one should cultivate: knowledge limited to food, restraint of the sense-doors, seeing danger in even the slightest fault, and practice (<s>yoga</s>) day and night. Then, wishing to dedicate even one's breathing for the benefit of others, one should rise in the fifth watch, properly complete the practices of excretion and the like, bathe in the manner appropriate to the central or border regions, take all destinies as one's support, generate the mind toward awakening through the <s>caturapramāṇa</s> (four immeasurables), in the presence of images of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels) sweep clean and scatter an abundance of fragrant flowers, and kneeling on the ground before them with palms joined, emanate innumerable and indescribable arrays of bodies in the presence of all <s>Buddhas</s>, all <s>Dharma</s>, and all <s>Mahāyāna Saṅgha</s> of the world-realms of the ten directions, and bow well at the feet of each one of them. One should worship them with immeasurable, vast, and boundless material offerings. Then, emanating from each body indescribable mouths and from each mouth indescribable tongues, one should confess all sins of self and others without remainder. One should rejoice in the merits of self and others. One should request those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> who have recently attained <s>abhisambodhi</s> (perfect awakening) to turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (wheel of Dharma). Those who, having turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, wish to relinquish the life-formations—one should pray that they not enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s> until the end of <s>saṃsāra</s>. One should dedicate all those wholesome roots toward <s>anuttara-samyak-sambodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). One should recite in full the individual verses as they appear in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: tataḥ saptapūjānantaraṃ sarvasattvān avalambya triśaraṇagamanapadāni triḥ paṭhet / tataḥ bodhicittamutpādayet, yathā vidhau prāpyate tathā ca kuryāt / antaśaśca evam-
body.translated_text: Then, after the seven offerings (<s>saptapūjā</s>), taking all sentient beings as one's support, one should recite the formula of the <s>triśaraṇagamana</s> (taking the three refuges) three times. Then one should generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), and should do so as obtained in the ritual. And at the very least, thus—

body.text:
buddhaṃ ca dharmañca gaṇottamaṃ ca
yāvaddhi bodhiṃ śaraṇaṃ gato 'smi /
dānādi-kṛtyaiśca kṛtairmayaibhiḥ
buddho bhaveyaṃ jagato hitāya // 2 // iti triḥ paṭhet /
body.translated_text:
To the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the supreme <s>Saṅgha</s>,
until awakening, I have gone for refuge.
By the merit of my deeds of giving and the like,
may I become a <s>Buddha</s> for the benefit of the world. // 2 // This should be recited three times.

body.text: tataḥ svakāyārpaṇaṃ, tataḥ mahāpuruṣāṇāṃ dharmanaye mahārathināṃ ca mārge avasthānāya pratijānīyāt / tataḥ svaśayyāyāṃ paryaṅkamābhujya gurubhaṭṭāraka-śrī-bodhibhadrakṛta-samādhi-(sambhāra) parivarttoktāninavāṅgāni jñātvā śamathavipaśyanāyogaṃ bhāvayet / so 'pi layauddhatyādisamastadoṣān prahāya bhāvanīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, the offering of one's own body; then one should vow to stand firm in the <s>Dharma</s> system of great beings and on the path of great chariot-masters (<s>mahārathins</s>). Then, sitting cross-legged on one's own bed, having understood the nine divisions taught in the <s>Samādhi-sambhāra-parivarta</s> composed by the venerable teacher Śrī <s>Bodhibhadra</s>, one should cultivate the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). This too should be practiced having abandoned all faults such as dullness (<s>laya</s>) and excitation (<s>auddhatya</s>).

body.text: tataḥ cakṣurunmīlya, niḥśvasya, bāhyābhyantaravastudarśane- 'aho! āścaryam, aho! āścaryam / ākāśopamānutpādataḥ pratītyasamutpādabalena nānābhāseyamavasthitiḥ ayam' aho! āścaryam' iti vicintya aṣṭamāyopamarupeṇa jānīyāt / tato mahākaruṇacittena samastādṛśyasattvebhyo dharmadeśanārtha yathābodhi mahāyāna-sūtrapāṭhaṃ kuryāt / tataḥ bhojanāvasare- 'ṣaṭtriṃśadaśuciparipūrṇena asāreṇa nāśaparyavasitena kāyenānena tadbuddhadharmakāya-sāramanveṣayāmi' iti vicintya na puṣṭyartha, nāpi rasāsaktayā yānadhiyā bhoktavyam / bhojanamātrāpi jñātavyā / aṣṭāṅgacikitsātantre-
body.translated_text: Then, opening the eyes and breathing out, upon seeing external and internal objects—'Ah, wonderful! Ah, wonderful! From non-arising like space, by the force of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), this manifold appearance, this state!'—'Ah, wonderful!'—reflecting thus, one should understand it in the manner of the eight similes of illusion. Then, with a mind of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), for the purpose of teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to all such unseen beings, one should recite <s>Mahāyāna sūtras</s> as appropriate for one's realization. Then, at mealtime—'With this body filled with thirty-six impurities, without essence, ending in destruction, I shall seek that essence which is the <s>Dharma-kāya</s> (truth-body) of the <s>Buddha</s>'—reflecting thus, one should eat not for the purpose of nourishment, nor with attachment to taste, but with the thought of it being a vehicle. One should also know the proper measure of food. In the <s>Aṣṭāṅgacikitsātantra</s> (Eight-limbed Medical Treatise)—

body.text:
annena kukṣerdvāvaṃśau pānenaikaṃ prapūrayet /
āśrayaṃ pavanādīnāṃ caturthamavaśeṣayet // 3 // iti /
body.translated_text:
Two parts of the belly should be filled with food, one with drink;
the fourth should be left as a support for wind and the like. // 3 //

body.text: tadbhojanaṃ caturbhāgeṣu vibhājyam / prathamo bhāgastriratnebhyo gurave cārpaṇīyaḥ / ekaṃ bhāgaṃ svayameva bhuñjīt / eko bhāgo bālebhyo 'nāthebhyaśca deyaḥ / ekaśca bhāgaḥ kukkurakākāditiryagbhyo deyaḥ / kaiściccaryāsaṅgraho 'nyathāpi kathitaḥ / anyo nayastu caryāsaṅgrahapradīpoktavat /
body.translated_text: That food should be divided into four portions. The first portion should be offered to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels) and the <s>Guru</s>. One portion should be eaten by oneself. One portion should be given to the poor and the destitute. And one portion should be given to animals such as dogs, crows, and the like. Some have described the <s>Caryāsaṅgraha</s> otherwise as well. But the other method is as stated in the <s>Caryāsaṅgrahapradīpa</s>.

body.text: tataḥ pūrvāhṇayāmeṣvapi pañcamaprahare yathoktavat sarvaṃ kāryam / madhyāhne sandhyāyāṃ rātreḥ prathame madhye ca yāme sarvathā yathoktāḥ sarve vidhayaḥ pūrayitavyāḥ / 'tādṛgyoginastasya nidrāśayanakālaniyamo nāsti' evaṃ guravo vadanti / tādṛgyoginaḥ sambhāramārgīyāḥ, mokṣamārgīyakuśalamūlotpādakāmaādikārmikā ahorātraṃ vyarthamanavasthitāḥ, tādṛgbhya āpattidoṣaḥ kathaṃ bhavet / yadi durvāsanābalād āpattirbhavet, evaṃ śīghram pratikuryāt /
body.translated_text: Then, during the forenoon watches also, in the fifth watch, everything should be done as previously described. At midday, at twilight, in the first and middle watches of the night—in every way all the prescribed rules should be fulfilled. 'For such a <s>yogin</s>, there is no fixed rule regarding the time of sleep and rest'—thus say the masters. Such <s>yogins</s> are on the <s>saṃbhāramārga</s> (path of accumulation); beginners who wish to produce the wholesome roots of the path of liberation, remaining day and night without wasting [time]—how could there be the fault of transgression for such persons? If, due to the force of bad habitual tendencies, a transgression does occur, one should quickly make amends.

body.text:
evaṃ teṣāṃ ṣaḍyāmānām aṣṭādaśadhā vibhāge kṛte sati catuḥpañcāśatkṣaṇā bhaviṣyanti /
bodhisattvā api uttamamadhyamā ('dhamāḥ) nava syuḥ / gurupadeśataḥ
pratipattyupāyān jānīyāt /
body.translated_text:
Thus, when the six watches are divided into eighteen parts, there will be fifty-four moments.
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> also may be of nine kinds: supreme, middling, and inferior [in three degrees]. One should know the methods of practice from the <s>guru's</s> instruction.

children.text: śreṣṭhaiḥ samākhyātatamaṃ sumārga bodhiprabhādyaiḥ kalitaśca śiṣyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That supreme and most excellent path proclaimed by the best, practiced by students headed by <s>Bodhiprabha</s>,

children.text: gattvā mahāyānakulābhijātaiḥ prāpyaṃ padaṃ tad dvipadendrakasya // 4 //
children.translated_text: attained by those born into the <s>Mahāyāna</s> family—that is the state of the Lord of Bipeds (the <s>Buddha</s>). // 4 //
The <s>Guru</s>, the venerable <s>Bodhisattva</s>, urged by the excellent monks headed by <s>Bodhiprabha</s>,
[this text was] translated by the monk <s>Jayaśīla</s>, a follower of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path. // 5 //

body.translated_text: The '<s>Bodhisattvādikarmikamārgāvatāradeśanā</s>' composed by <s>Ācārya Dīpaṅkaraśrījñāna</s> is completed.

body.text: tenaiva paṇḍitena lokacakṣuṣā ca jayaśīlena anūditā //
body.translated_text: Translated by that same <s>paṇḍita</s> and by <s>Jayaśīla</s>, the eye of the world.
